title: Safe Isolation Verification
summary: Safe Isolation Verification matters because failure to properly isolate and verify equipment before work begins is one of the most common causes of serious electrical and mechanical incidents.
talking_points: Identify all energy sources (electrical, mechanical, pressure, gravity).
Isolate and lock out with your own padlock and tag.
Prove the isolation is effective before starting work.
Remove your lock only when your work is complete and it is safe to do so.
Never rely on someone else's isolation without applying your own lock.
Tag isolators with your name and the date.
If something goes wrong: if equipment energizes unexpectedly, stop work and isolate again immediately; report the failure; do not resume until the cause is identified and corrected.
site_hazards_to_check: Multiple people working without coordinated lock out
